subject: Clarify billing units for Chat vs Responses and legacy endpoints
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightline-retail.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rate card question — Chat v Responses v legacy endpoints

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team at Brightline liked the latency numbers. Before we get into commercials, procurement is asking for a clear mapping between the different endpoint types and how we will be billed. Specifically:

- How do Chat Completions (new chat API) and Responses (response-style API) map to billing units?
- How do those compare to the legacy /v1/chat/completions and /v1/completions endpoints in our invoices?
- If we send a streaming chat (partial tokens + function calls) vs a single response call, is there a different unit calc?

We expect ~40M tokens/month initially, with bursts up to 150k tokens/min during peak campaigns. Also: are there transparent thresholds for volume discounts and how they apply across endpoint types?

Can you share a short example mapping (input tokens, output tokens -> billed units) and any rate card or worksheet you have?

Appreciate it — Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Partnerships | Brightline Retail
[sent from mobile]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightline-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rate card question — Chat v Responses v legacy endpoints

Hi Samantha — great to hear the demo landed well. Quick summary before I attach our rate card:

1) High-level mapping:
   - "Chat Completions" (new chat API): billed per token (input + output) using the Chat unit in the ratecard. Continuous streaming is billed identically — tokens billed as emitted.
   - "Responses" (response-style API): also token-based, but optimized pricing for short calls (we apply a small per-request credit that benefits request-heavy patterns).
   - "Legacy endpoints" (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions): legacy SKU mapping still appears on invoices for older integrations; we map those sessions to the closest modern SKU on new contracts (we provided a mapping table in the attached sheet).

2) Streaming vs single-call: tokens are what matter — whether streamed or not. Function-call metadata (tool call payloads) can add a fixed small overhead per tool invocation; we can quantify that for your expected usage.

3) Discounts: volume tiers are applied to total token spend across hosted APIs. For multi-endpoint usage we consolidate tokens into a single bucket for discount calculations. There are also commit-based discounts for Dedicated if you want to reserve capacity.

I've attached: redwood_ratecard_v2.pdf and an example_payload_token_counts.csv with sample mappings. Marissa (cc'd) will follow up with a worked example applied to your 40M token/month baseline and provide threshold pricing.

Next step: Marissa will send a short table mapping a few sample interactions (chat with 120 tokens in + 300 out, response-style 20 in + 80 out, legacy completion 30 in + 70 out) to billed units and dollars. Any other input (e.g., ratio of short vs long calls) helps.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Rate card question — Chat v Responses v legacy endpoints

Thanks Priya — that helps. A couple of clarifying points from procurement:

- Can you confirm the percent overhead you apply for function-call metadata (we do a lot of product attribute lookups via tools; average ~2 tool calls per end user request).
- For discounted tiers: do discounts apply to each token equally, or are some SKUs (e.g., embeddings) excluded from the same discount band?
- For streaming large outputs (e.g., >2k tokens in response), are there any soft caps or throttles that change pricing behavior?

Also: for the 40M token baseline, we'd like an illustrative invoice line item showing how that becomes dollars under the standard hosted rate and under a ~20% committed discount tier. Procurement would like to see a one-page PDF to hand to finance.

If you can get that before Friday, that would be ideal.

—Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Partnerships
Brightline Retail

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@brightline-retail.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rate card question — Chat v Responses v legacy endpoints

Hi Samantha — attaching the worked example and shortone-pager you asked for. Key answers inline below and a worked example at the bottom.

- Function-call overhead: we add a small per-tool-invocation overhead that equates to ~0.5% of token billing on typical payloads (this is rounded and depends on tool payload size). For your ~2 tool calls per request average, assume an extra ~1% delta to token spend. We can run precise estimates if you share sample tool payloads.
- Discount applicability: hosted API token spend is the primary base for volume discounts. Embeddings and other add-ons are generally included in the tier calculations unless explicitly excluded in a bespoke contract. We call out exceptions in the ratecard; the attached PDF highlights standard inclusions.
- Streaming large outputs: no special throttle that changes billing; tokens billed as emitted. There are safety/throughput protections at very high sustained QPS — those do not alter per-token pricing, but may require rate limits for stability.

Worked example (from attached spreadsheet):
- Baseline (no commit): 40,000,000 tokens/month 
  - Standard hosted rate: $0.0006 per token -> $24,000/month
- With 20% committed discount: effective rate $0.00048 per token -> $19,200/month
- Add tool-call overhead estimate (1%): +$192/month (after discount)

Notes: legacy /v1 SKUs will be remapped on new invoices; historical line items remain for audit but future billing uses the modern SKU names. If you want an explicit line-by-line mock invoice with those legacy labels included for your auditors, we can produce that as well.

Attachments: short_invoice_example_brightline.pdf (one page) and worked_rate_table_brightline.csv

Next steps:
- If you confirm the 40M baseline and that ~2 tool calls/request is representative, I will generate a mock invoice and a HubSpot deal update with commit options (monthly commit / annual commit).
- If you'd like, Vivek (cc) can run one-off tokenization on sample payloads to give a tighter tool-call overhead estimate.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Pricing Manager
Redwood Inference
